code:
CONSTANTS co_object TYPE c LENGTH 10 VALUE 'ZORDER'.
CONSTANTS co_change TYPE c LENGTH 2 VALUE '02'.
allowed = abap_false.
AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT co_object
  ID 'ACTVT' FIELD co_change
  ID 'BUKRS' FIELD company_code.
IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.
allowed = abap_true.
title: Check the change permission before acting
intro: A denied check leaves the result false.
context: Method body of a boolean authorization helper with IMPORTING company_code TYPE bukrs and RETURNING VALUE(allowed) TYPE abap_bool. Prerequisite: custom authorization object ZORDER already exists with exactly ACTVT and BUKRS and appropriate role values. The caller must reject false before any protected work.
outcome: With company_code 1000, a display-only user remains denied; a user authorized for activity 02 in company 1000 passes this check.
caveat: This helper only evaluates permission; it performs no business write. Do not trust a caller-supplied company without resolving it from the protected object. Framework operations still need their own authorization response contract.

highlights.label: Check the requested operation
highlights.explanation: The result starts false. ACTVT 02 checks change permission, not display permission.

highlights.label: Use the result immediately
highlights.explanation: No intervening statement can overwrite sy-subrc. Every nonzero result returns false.

code:
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_change,
         changed_at TYPE timestamp,
         order_id   TYPE i,
       END OF ty_change.
DATA lt_changes TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_change
  WITH UNIQUE KEY changed_at order_id.
lt_changes = VALUE #(
  ( changed_at = '20261013090000' order_id = 7 )
  ( changed_at = '20261013090000' order_id = 9 )
  ( changed_at = '20261013090100' order_id = 10 ) ).
CONSTANTS co_after_time TYPE timestamp VALUE '20261013090000'.
CONSTANTS co_after_id TYPE i VALUE 7.
CONSTANTS co_upper_time TYPE timestamp VALUE '20261013090100'.
CONSTANTS co_page_size TYPE i VALUE 2.
DATA lt_page TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_change WITH EMPTY KEY.
LOOP AT lt_changes INTO DATA(ls_change)
  WHERE ( changed_at > co_after_time OR
        ( changed_at = co_after_time AND order_id > co_after_id ) )
    AND changed_at <= co_upper_time.
  APPEND ls_change TO lt_page.
  IF lines( lt_page ) = co_page_size.
    EXIT.
  ENDIF.
ENDLOOP.
title: Keep the second record with the same timestamp
intro: Continue after the timestamp and ID together.
context: Self-contained method-body illustration with fixed UTC timestamp fixtures in an internal table. It demonstrates a continuation predicate and a two-row page, not database extraction or a live cursor.
outcome: lt_page contains orders 9 and 10 in that order. Order 9 is retained even though its timestamp equals the checkpoint timestamp.
caveat: The source is frozen in memory. Translating this to SQL requires the same deterministic ORDER BY, a bounded row limit, suitable indexes and a source-specific delta contract. It does not solve late commits, deletes or concurrent changes.

highlights.label: Define a stable order
highlights.explanation: The key sorts by changed_at, then order_id. Orders 7 and 9 share a timestamp.

highlights.label: Continue after the complete pair
highlights.explanation: Equal timestamps are included when their ID exceeds 7. The fixed upper time bounds this run.

highlights.label: Keep the page bounded
highlights.explanation: Stop after two rows: 9 and 10. Advance the extraction checkpoint after the page and continuation are durably staged atomically, or after downstream confirmation if there is no durable stage. Delivery has its own state.

code:
CLASS lcl_total DEFINITION FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES ty_values TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY.
    CLASS-METHODS calculate IMPORTING lt_values TYPE ty_values
      RETURNING VALUE(total) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.
CLASS lcl_total IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD calculate.
    total = REDUCE i( INIT sum = 0
      FOR number IN lt_values NEXT sum = sum + number ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
CLASS ltc_total DEFINITION FINAL FOR TESTING
  DURATION SHORT RISK LEVEL HARMLESS.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA lt_values TYPE lcl_total=>ty_values.
    METHODS setup.
    METHODS adds_values FOR TESTING.
    METHODS empty_is_zero FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.
CLASS ltc_total IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD setup.
    lt_values = VALUE #( ( 40 ) ( 60 ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD adds_values.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lcl_total=>calculate( lt_values ) exp = 100 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD empty_is_zero.
    CLEAR lt_values.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lcl_total=>calculate( lt_values ) exp = 0 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
title: Fresh input for each calculator test
intro: Both test orders must give the same results.
context: Complete local teaching class and ABAP Unit test class, placed in a suitable local class/test include. Requires a release supporting REDUCE and inline constructor expressions. Fixture integers are unitless and deliberately small.
outcome: adds_values expects 100. empty_is_zero expects 0. setup restores 40 and 60 before each test, so clearing one test input cannot affect the other.
caveat: No database or remote call is made. No teardown is needed for this local-only fixture. HARMLESS describes that design; changing the tested code to write real data would require a new isolation and risk review.

highlights.label: Test the real calculation
highlights.explanation: The empty input returns the initial sum 0; otherwise the actual values are added.

highlights.label: Reset before each test
highlights.explanation: The test framework runs setup separately before both test methods.

highlights.label: Check normal and empty input
highlights.explanation: The assertions verify 100 and 0. Neither test relies on the other running first.
